name: QuickBooks Online
tagline: Small-business accounting, invoicing, expenses, payroll add-ons, and tax workflows

pricing.notes: Official Intuit pricing checked 2026-07-30; Simple Start standard monthly price shown around $38/month, excluding time-limited promos.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 user; 1 bank institution; 2 invoices/month; 1 estimate/month; 2 receipt uploads/month; 1 contractor; 3 reports; 5 trips/month; 0 accountant seats
tiers.notes: Enabling QuickBooks Payments unlocks unlimited invoices but introduces processing fees.

tiers.name: Simple Start
tiers.limits: 1 user + 2 accountants; 250 chart-of-account entries; 1 custom field; 1 sales channel; 25 AI questions/month

tiers.name: Essentials
tiers.limits: 3 users + 2 accountants; 250 accounts; 4 custom fields; 3 sales channels; 25 AI questions/month

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: 5 users + 2 accountants; 40 classes/locations; 250 accounts; 4 custom fields; unlimited sales channels; 25 AI questions/month

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: 25 users + 3 accountants; unlimited classes/locations and accounts; 12 custom fields; 25 AI questions/month; Bill Pay Elite included

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 user, 1 bank institution, 2 invoices/month, 1 estimate/month, 2 receipts/month, 1 contractor, 3 reports, and 5 trips/month
pricing.hiddenCosts: The current 90%-off-for-3-months offer expires August 27, 2026 and then resets to list price. Standard ACH charges $0.50 after included allowances; Bill Pay Elite is $45/month on lower plans; enhanced inventory is $40/month on Simple Start/Essentials; payment processing and payroll are separate.

verdictSummary: You can build invoicing and expense tables, but QuickBooks' value is accounting correctness, bank feeds, payroll/tax ecosystem, accountant workflows, compliance, and support.
coreLoopDIY: For simple needs, build invoice creation, payment tracking, expenses, CSV bank import, and basic P&L reports.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because accounting mistakes and tax messes cost more than the subscription.

priorArt.name: Akaunting
priorArt.desc: Open-source accounting software for invoicing, expenses, and small-business books.

alternatives.name: ERPNext
alternatives.desc: A real accounting ERP with invoices, expenses, reconciliation, inventory and payroll; setup is a small IT department in miniature.

facts.install: Managed Frappe Cloud signup, or the supported Frappe Docker/Bench deployment
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted companies live in MariaDB site databases with site files and attachments on the server; managed-hosting data lives in the selected Frappe Cloud site.
facts.gapVsPaid: ERPNext is much harder to deploy and does not deliver QuickBooks' turnkey US bank feeds, payroll add-ons, tax workflows, payments, and accountant ecosystem out of the box.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting is an ERP deployment rather than a desktop install: Docker or Bench, MariaDB, Redis, workers, a reverse proxy, backups, upgrades, and country-specific accounting setup.

alternatives.name: Manager Desktop
alternatives.desc: A complete desktop ledger with invoices, reconciliation, expenses and inventory; teamwork stops at the file.

facts.install: Native desktop installer for Windows, macOS, or Linux
facts.dataFormat: Each business is stored in a local .manager file backed by SQLite, including its accounting records and attached documents; the user chooses and backs up that file.
facts.gapVsPaid: Its local business file is effectively single-user and lacks QuickBooks' live collaboration, managed bank feeds, payroll, payments, and tax-service ecosystem.

alternatives.name: Bigcapital
alternatives.desc: Modern double-entry books, bills, expenses and inventory in Docker; bank feeds are still your problem to arrange.

facts.install: Official server setup script and Docker-based deployment
facts.dataFormat: Books, contacts, invoices, bills, inventory, and settings live in the deployment's MariaDB database, with generated files and attachments on configured server storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: It lacks QuickBooks' plug-and-play bank connections, payroll and tax services, payments network, and accountant ecosystem, while making you operate the server.
facts.setupBlocker: It needs a Linux server, Docker, DNS and HTTPS, database and mail configuration, backups, and upgrades; the hosted product is not the indefinitely free path.

alternatives.name: LedgerSMB
alternatives.desc: Serious double-entry accounting with quotes, stock, projects and reports; the interface does not audition for lifestyle ads.

facts.install: Docker Compose is the shortest documented path; packages and manual Perl installation also exist
facts.dataFormat: Companies and accounting records live in PostgreSQL databases; uploaded or generated documents live in the configured document store or server volumes.
facts.gapVsPaid: LedgerSMB is capable accounting software but lacks QuickBooks' polished bank-feed, payments, payroll, tax, mobile, and accountant-integration experience.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is a real web stack, Docker, PostgreSQL, administrator credentials, a reverse proxy and TLS for internet use, plus backups and upgrades.

alternatives.name: Frappe Books
alternatives.desc: Local books with invoices, bills, payments and a real ledger; collaboration ends where the SQLite file begins.

facts.install: Native desktop installer; Homebrew and Flatpak paths are also published
facts.dataFormat: Each company is a local SQLite .db file selected by the user, with its ledger, invoices, bills, and related records in that file.
facts.gapVsPaid: The SQLite company file is local and collaboration-light, with no comparable managed bank feeds, payroll, tax filing, payments, or accountant network.

alternatives.name: Odoo Accounting (One App Free)
alternatives.desc: A full hosted accounting app for zero dollars; install one unrelated Odoo app and the free ride ends.

facts.install: Create an Odoo Online database and select Accounting as the single free app
facts.dataFormat: Accounting records and attachments live in the Odoo Online database and filestore operated by Odoo; the internal storage format is not exposed to the hosted user.
facts.gapVsPaid: The zero-dollar deal ends when another priced Odoo app is installed, while payroll, country-specific tax workflows, and some bank integrations still require configuration or additional products.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is configuring the correct country localization, chart of accounts, taxes, journals, and bank import; installing any additional priced Odoo app ends One App Free eligibility.

alternatives.name: Dolibarr
alternatives.desc: Invoices, banking, stock and double-entry books in one practical suite; payroll is explicitly not invited.

facts.install: DoliWamp, DoliDeb, DoliRPM, Docker, or a conventional PHP web-server installation
facts.dataFormat: Business records live in MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL, while uploaded and generated documents live in Dolibarr's documents directory or mounted volume.
facts.gapVsPaid: Dolibarr explicitly does not provide payroll and does not match QuickBooks' managed US bank-feed, tax, payments, and accountant ecosystem.
facts.setupBlocker: A packaged desktop-style installer exists on some platforms, but a durable deployment still needs a web server or Docker, database, HTTPS, backups, updates, and localization.

alternatives.name: GnuCash
alternatives.desc: Industrial-strength double entry, invoicing and reports on a desktop; friendly is not one of the accounting standards.

facts.install: Native desktop installer or operating-system package
facts.dataFormat: The default book is a local compressed XML .gnucash file; SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL backends are optional, but the documentation warns that database storage does not make GnuCash a true multi-user application.
facts.gapVsPaid: GnuCash is a manual, single-user desktop workflow with no QuickBooks-equivalent managed bank feeds, online collaboration, payroll, payments, or tax automation.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Akaunting
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free base is single-entry unless you buy the Double-Entry app, and the repo is BSL rather than open source.

notes: Essential no/kinda: the UI is cloneable, financial trust is not.
prompt:
Build me a bookkeeping-lite app covering the safe personal slice of QuickBooks
Online: invoicing a few clients and tracking expenses. Requirements:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, binds to localhost, no
  hosting.
- Invoices: client, line items, tax rate, due date; render to PDF with
  Playwright's page.pdf; a manual mark-paid flag.
- Expenses: import my bank's CSV export, categorize with a rules table that
  auto-matches repeat payees, edit the rest by hand.
- Reports: a cash-basis P&L and per-quarter totals, plus CSV export of
  everything for the accountant.
- No accounts, no telemetry, the books never leave my machine; write a nightly
  dated backup copy of the SQLite file.
- Out of scope: bank feeds, reconciliation, payroll, and anything that files
  taxes. Do not build tax logic of any kind.
- README: state plainly that this is bookkeeping-lite, not accounting.
  QuickBooks' real product is accounting correctness, bank feeds, and the
  accountant ecosystem, none of which this rebuilds; when the numbers start to
  matter, the honest move is real software or an accountant.
